links.outcome: Patient trust in and choice of AI visits by attributes including governance, clinician presence, data quality
links.effect: Clinician presence AMCE 0.184; FDA approval 0.111; AI performance above specialist 0.325. Disclosed information on governance, data and performance influenced choice, but this is not disclosure of AI use itself.
links.quote: Increasing transparency regarding these attributes may increase patient trust and consent to incorporating AI in their care.

links.outcome: Effect of disclosing representative versus biased training data on patient choice and trust
links.effect: Representative US dataset vs no information: AMCE 0.119 (95% CI 0.106-0.131); biased dataset was neither favored nor disfavored vs no information.
links.quote: Respondents preferred AI trained on a representative US population dataset to AI about which they received no training data information (AMCE, 0.119; 95% CI, 0.106 to 0.131).

links.effect: Local hospital certification increased preference (AMCE, 0.078 [95% CI, 0.068 to 0.088]) vs uncertified.
links.quote: The increase for local hospital certification (AMCE, 0.078 [95% CI, 0.068 to 0.088]) was smaller (difference between local and FDA, 0.033 [95% CI, 0.019 to 0.047]; P < .001; difference between local and Mayo Clinic, 0.034 [95% CI, 0.020 to 0.048]; P < .001).

links.effect: FDA approval increased preference (AMCE, 0.111 [95% CI, 0.101 to 0.121]) vs unapproved.
links.quote: The increases in preference associated with FDA approval (AMCE, 0.111 [95% CI, 0.101 to 0.121]) and Mayo Clinic certification (AMCE, 0.111 [95% CI, 0.101 to 0.121]) were the same size (difference, 0 [95% CI, −0.014 to 0.014]; P = .96).

links.effect: Clinician presence increased probability of choosing the AI visit by 18.4% (95% CI, 17.3%-19.5%) vs no clinician.
links.quote: The AMCE was 0.184 (95% CI, 0.173-0.195), meaning that respondents were 18.4% (95% CI, 17.3%-19.5%) more likely to choose a visit with a clinician than one with no clinician (baseline).

screen.practice: governance certification, human-in-the-loop clinician oversight, and data disclosure
screen.reason: The study empirically tests via a discrete choice / conjoint experiment how specific deployment practices and safeguards (clinician-in-the-loop oversight, regulatory/institutional certification/governance, and data quality disclosure) impact patient trust and preference for AI-assisted diagnostic encounters.
